Alger, 8 novembre 2026 (Algeria Tech) —: Algiers, November 8, 2026 (Algeria Tech) — Algeria is holding advanced discussions with the World Bank to secure funding for local innovative companies. This announcement by Minister Noureddine Ouadah comes ahead of the fifth African Startup Conference, scheduled from December 5 to 7 in Algiers.
Des discussions avancées avec la Banque: Advanced discussions with the World Bank
Le gouvernement algérien négocie un sout: The Algerian government is negotiating financial support from the World Bank to benefit the country's innovative companies. According to statements by the Minister of Knowledge Economy, Startups and Micro-enterprises, Noureddine Ouadah, these efforts aim to mobilize more than 10 million dollars for several local startups. Discussions are at a well-advanced stage with the financial institution, which has expressed interest in high-growth players capable of expanding into Africa and Europe.
L'annonce s'inscrit dans le cadre des pr: The announcement is part of the preparations for the fifth edition of the African Startup Conference, organized from December 5 to 7 in the Algerian capital. This event will bring together over 25,000 participants and 40 African ministerial delegations. Discussions will focus primarily on advanced technologies applied to key sectors such as energy, health, artificial intelligence, agriculture, and food, while addressing digital sovereignty issues.
La Deep Tech au centre des enjeux africa: Deep Tech at the heart of African challenges
Placée sous le thème de la technologie p: Placed under the theme of deep technology, this international meeting aims to boost investments towards the continent. According to figures from the United Nations Development Programme cited by the minister, funding injected into Deep Tech in Africa has seen major growth over recent years.

The ministerial summit organized during previous gatherings resulted in resolutions adopted by the African Union. Furthermore, the conclusions formulated during the fourth edition were validated at the headquarters of the international organization in Addis Ababa.
